subject: Life Sciences
topic: Hominid fossils and South African discoveries

items.q: A foramen magnum positioned forward, under the skull, indicates that a hominid:
items.qAf: ’n Foramen magnum wat vorentoe, onder die skedel, geleë is, dui aan dat ’n hominied:
optionsAf: regop op twee bene geloop het
items.explain: The spinal cord enters from below when the body is upright — bipedalism.
items.explainAf: Die rugmurg gaan van onder in die skedel in wanneer die liggaam regop is — tweevoetigheid.

items.q: Compared with Australopithecus, Homo sapiens has:
items.qAf: In vergelyking met Australopithecus het Homo sapiens:
options: a larger cranium and smaller brow ridges
a smaller cranium and larger brow ridges
items.explain: Trends: larger brain, flatter face, reduced brow ridges and jaws.
items.explainAf: Tendense: groter brein, platter gesig, kleiner wenkbrouriwwe en kakebene.

items.q: A hominid’s brain volume increased from 450 cm³ to 1 350 cm³. The percentage increase is:
items.qAf: ’n Hominied se breinvolume het van 450 cm³ tot 1 350 cm³ toegeneem. Die persentasietoename is:

items.q: The Taung Child, found in South Africa, is a fossil of:
items.qAf: Die Taung-kind, wat in Suid-Afrika gevind is, is ’n fossiel van:
items.explain: The Taung Child (1924) was the first Australopithecus africanus fossil described.
items.explainAf: Die Taung-kind (1924) was die eerste Australopithecus africanus-fossiel wat beskryf is.

items.q: Engraved ochre and shell beads at Blombos Cave are evidence of:
items.qAf: Gegraveerde oker en skulpkrale by Blomboskrot is bewys van:
options: symbolic thinking in early modern humans
optionsAf: simboliese denke by vroeë moderne mense
items.explain: Decorated objects show abstract, symbolic behaviour.
items.explainAf: Versierde voorwerpe wys abstrakte, simboliese gedrag.

items.q: Burnt bone and ash deep inside Wonderwerk Cave provide some of the oldest evidence of:
items.qAf: Verbrande been en as diep binne Wonderwerkgrot lewer van die oudste bewyse van:
items.explain: Wonderwerk shows controlled fire about a million years ago.
items.explainAf: Wonderwerk wys beheerde vuur ongeveer ’n miljoen jaar gelede.

items.q: The site near Johannesburg known as the Cradle of Humankind, where Mrs Ples was found.
items.qAf: Die terrein naby Johannesburg bekend as die Wieg van die Mensdom, waar Mrs Ples gevind is.

items.q: The species name of the Taung Child fossil.
The hominid species described from the Rising Star cave system in 2015.
items.qAf: Die hominiedspesie wat in 2015 uit die Rising Star-grotstelsel beskryf is.

items.q: The scientist who described the Taung Child in 1925.
items.qAf: Die wetenskaplike wat die Taung-kind in 1925 beskryf het.

items.text: Little Foot is an almost complete [[]] skeleton found at Sterkfontein. Australopithecus sediba was found at [[]] in 2008.
items.textAf: Little Foot is ’n byna volledige [[]]-skelet wat by Sterkfontein gevind is. Australopithecus sediba is in 2008 by [[]] gevind.

items.q: The Taung Child was the first Australopithecus fossil to be described.
items.qAf: Die Taung-kind was die eerste Australopithecus-fossiel wat beskryf is.
items.explain: True. Raymond Dart named Australopithecus africanus from it in 1925.
items.explainAf: Waar. Raymond Dart het Australopithecus africanus in 1925 daarvolgens benoem.

items.q: Homo naledi had a brain as large as that of modern humans.
items.qAf: Homo naledi het ’n brein so groot soos dié van moderne mense gehad.
items.explain: False. Homo naledi had a small brain, about a third the size of ours.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Homo naledi het ’n klein brein gehad, omtrent ’n derde van die grootte van ons s’n.

items.q: Match each fossil or discovery in column A with its site in column B.
items.qAf: Pas elke fossiel of ontdekking in kolom A by sy terrein in kolom B.

items.q: Explain why the Cradle of Humankind is important in the study of human evolution.
items.qAf: Verduidelik waarom die Wieg van die Mensdom belangrik is in die studie van menslike evolusie.
points: It has a large number of hominid fossils from several species, spanning millions of years.
The fossils support the idea that hominids evolved in Africa (Out of Africa).
pointsAf: Dit het ’n groot aantal hominiedfossiele van verskeie spesies, oor miljoene jare.
Die fossiele ondersteun die idee dat hominiede in Afrika ontwikkel het (Uit Afrika).
